Q: KingswaySoft Salesforce Destination v26.2 – What does “Assume Success on Accepted Job” actually do? A:

Yes, your deduction is spot on.

Basically it turns the Bulk API write into an asynchronous fire-and-forget operation from SSIS's perspective.

Normally, KingswaySoft uploads the batch and then sits there in a polling loop waiting for Salesforce to finish processing all rows (`JobComplete`) so it can grab the new SalesforceRecordIds and route any bad rows to the error output.

When you check **"Assume Success on Accepted Job"**, the component sends the data, waits until Salesforce says "okay, job accepted and queued in InProgress/UploadComplete", and then the SSIS data flow task finishes immediately and turns green.

### When to actually use it:

- **Large datasets:** If your bulk load takes 45+ mins inside Salesforce because of heavy triggers/flows, you probably dont want your SSIS worker thread sitting blocked the whole time.

- **Saving API limits:** It avoids constant polling requests against your 24hr API limit while Salesforce crunches through the queue.

### Important gotchas / side effects to watch out for:

1. **`SalesforceRecordId` will be blank / NULL** in your downstream pipeline components because the job hasnt actually created the records yet when SSIS finishes.

2. **No row-level error handling:** If 20 rows fail in Salesforce later due to validation rules or required fields, your SSIS package will still show success and the SSIS error output wont catch them.

3. You'll need to check the Salesforce Bulk Data Load Jobs page manually (or write a separate reconciliation query task later) to see if any records failed.

Q: Ambisonic Recordings and RealityKit A:

Ambisonics

To implement ambisonic multi-channel audio in RealityKit for Xcode 27/26/25, you need to use the AmbientAudioComponent. You'd be aware that each channel of your ambisonic sound file is anchored to a fixed direction (orientation). Spatial position isn't taken into account in this case.

@available(visionOS 1.0, macOS 15.0, iOS 18.0, tvOS 26.0, *)
public struct AmbientAudioComponent

There's no distance attenuation. This means the sound volume doesn't drop as the user moves further from the source entity unlike what happens when using SpatialAudioComponent. And there's no environmental reverberation.

Here's the code:

let sound = Entity()

RealityView { rvcc in
    if let resource = try? await AudioFileResource(named: "ambisonic") {
        sound.components[AmbientAudioComponent.self] = .init(gain: -15)
        sound.playAudio(resource)                        // controller
        rvcc.add(sound)
    }
}

It should also be noted that ambient audio source takes into account not only the relative orientation of the source itself but also the listener's orientation.

Q: How to build a function that takes more arguments with each iteration A:

Another answer here has built this incredibly smart solution by exploiting the intrinsics of Booleans. I can only convince myself in its validity by induction, though have no idea how one could come up with such a non-obvious and downright mysterious approach.

P0 = <T,F>
P1 = <KT,P0> 
OR1 a = P0 a = a T F = a
P2 = <K(KT),P1>
OR2 a b = P1 a b = a (KT) P0 b
                 = a T (P0 b)   = a T b
OR3 a b c = P2 a b c = a (K(KT)) P1 b c
                 = a T (P1 b c) = a T (OR2 b c)
........

This uses the standard K combinator, K = λab.a, and pairs <a,b> = λz.zab such that K a b = a and <a,b> c = c a b.

Or maybe, start with the recursive equation

M := N+1
ORM a b c ... 
   = a T (ORN b c ...)
   = a (TN b c ...) (ORN b c ...)
   = a TN ORN b c ...
   = <TN,ORN> a b c      !
; and so,
ORM   = <TN,ORN>

and this way get there. Still it's pretty clever and non-obvious.

I would like to find the easy solution here, easy to come up with and easy to understand. You said iteration, you said Church numerals. First,

TN n a b c ... 
    = n G Z a b c ...              ;; for some G,Z
    = G(G(...(GZ)...)) a b c ...   ;; that should be
  ;;  G r              a      = r
    =   G(...(GZ)...)    b c ...   ;; so G is K
    = K(G(...(GZ)...)) a b c ...   ;; and Z is T
    = K(K(...(KT)...)) a b c ...
    = n K T a b c ...

TN = λn.n K T

is self-evident. The important bit is that Church numerals are folds over implicit lists of ignored elements.

Applying the same exploratory approach,

ORN n a b c ... 
   = G(G(...(GZ)...)) F a b c ...
   =   G(...(GZ)...) (F|a) b c ...
   =    (...(GZ)...) ((F|a)|b) c ...

ORN = λn. n (λrab.r(OR a b)) I F

should be just as self-evident. It is not "smart," but it is simple, self-evidently correct, and demonstrates a standard way to approach such problems in general.

Here again the standard definitions are used, the identity combinator I = λx.x, the Boolean False F = λab.b which is the identity of the OR operation, and whatever the definition of the standard binary OR operation you'd prefer.

Q: Eclipse Generic Code Editor uses the wrong TextMate grammar A:

I solved the problem by hacking the Eclipse installation config files to remove the bundled Objective-C TextMate bundled so that it can no longer block my newly added Mumps configuration for .m files.

This is not optional. There should be some official GUI way to solve this. I will not mark this answer as accepted awaiting such a solution.

Instructions:

  1. In the root Eclipse IDE installation directory, locate the file eclipse/plugins/org.eclipse.tm4e.language_pack_0.18.0.202608200919.jar

  2. Inside the jar file, edit plugin.xml to remove the sections for Objective-C and Objective-C++.

  3. Inside the jar file, delete the directory syntaxes/objective-c.

  4. In the root installation directory, delete the directory eclipse/configuration/org.eclipse.core.runtime. There is some cache in this directory that remembers the unmodified plugin.xml. If this is not done an error is generated with a .m file is opened because. The directory is recreated on program startup.

Finished!

Q: How to take reports form AVEVA E3D using C# A:

There is a possibility to use .net( ReportingAddin.dll ) as well as pml object for automation purpose. The preliminary requirement is to have report defination file setup using AVEVA report designer.

  import 'ReportingAddin'
  handle any
  endhandle

  using namespace 'Aveva.Core.Reporting'
  !report                     = object PMLReport()

  !report.EXPORTASXLSX(|C:\db\PipeReport.repv|, |C:\db\Output.xlsx| )

-- For more information about !report you can use below command
  q var !report.methods()
